brief: NDX printed a hammer candle at the trend line held since the April lows, converging with the 100-day moving average, making this level a must-hold for tech. A hold could trigger a powerful squeeze, a break could get ugly fast. Rising tech credit spreads are now moving with falling tech stocks, unlike an earlier episode when a CDS spike coincided with a rallying NDX. SMH and DRAM saw their highest volumes in some time as long/short books aggressively de-grossed. Global systematic long/short fell 1.4% in a nearly four-standard-deviation move, which the note frames as a gross-exposure unwind rather than a net-exposure one, with one proposed relative-value trade of shorting hyperscalers versus semis. The most-leveraged parts of the AI complex reversed sharply off yesterday's lows, suggesting credit fears may have been overdone short term, though the structural mismatch between capital and power-ready AI compute capacity remains and could reprice gradually or violently. Spot GPU rental rates stay strong despite depreciation. NDX and the 10-year yield have moved together since September, implying growth concerns now dominate over the usual discount-rate effect. NDX forward P/E is back near 21x, a level revisited multiple times since the AI cycle began in 2023.
